messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: streaming-latency-p99 breach detected in pool=prod-shared-gpu-3 · metric=streaming.request_duration.p99 · value=3.8s · SLO(p99)=2.0s · paging oncall: @oncall-anna :rotating_light:
oncall-anna: I'm on it, paging SREs. Observed user reports about token gaps and stalls for calls routed to prod-shared-gpu-3. Starting triage.
sre-miguel: grabbing logs. Any sign of a rollout or config change in the last 30m?
infra-ryan: no deploys in the window per deploy-bot. I see elevated block_io wait and cgroup throttling on a subset of nodes. Running quick checks now.
ml-olivia: which models are hot? Could be a heavy kv-cache or long-context run from a tenant.
support-lina: Customer-facing: multiple tickets from Tenant:Songbird about streaming stalls at ~12:20 UTC. They report intermittent long gaps between tokens (~2-4s). Ticket IDs: #4321, #4329. Lane flagged as P1.
ops-bot: Auto-mitigation candidate: enable fallback-model-route for streaming to dedup variant with lower KV usage. Requires approval.
oncall-anna: miguel/ryan — can you post p95/p99 numbers per model + nodes? We need scope (single tenant vs pool-wide).
sre-miguel: quick metrics: pool=prod-shared-gpu-3 · overall p95=820ms, p99=3.8s. streaming stalls count increased x18 in last 10m. Top offending model: gpt-small-q4 (but it has most traffic). Breaking down by tenant: tenant-songbird ~47% of requests to the pool, tenant-lumen ~12%.
infra-ryan: on node-gpu-38 (in that pool) iostat shows high average await and high write IO. cgroup stats: blkio.throttle.io_service_bytes: frequent throttles. nvml (nvidia-smi) shows GPU SM usage moderate but memory bandwidth spiking on some processes. suspect noisy neighbor causing IO contention (checkpointing / logging spikes).
ml-olivia: songbird recently started long-context analysis (12k tokens) in production last week. That explains KV cache pressure and increased IO when cache miss + spool to disk occurs.
ops-bot: suggested mitigation list: 1) migrate heavy tenants off pool 2) increase cgroup blkio limits temporarily 3) enable model fallback 4) cordon affected nodes 5) throttle tenant concurrency.
sre-miguel: action: I'll try to throttle tenant-songbird concurrency (limit to 2 concurrent streams) to immediately reduce pressure. Applying token-level rate limit in routing rules now.
support-lina: notifying Songbird contacts that we're investigating and may throttle traffic temporarily; preparing runbook message.
infra-ryan: I'll run: 
```
ssh infra@gpu-38
sudo cat /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/docker/<container-id>/blkio.throttle.io_service_bytes
iostat -x 1 3
```
Seeing heavy write waits on nvme, secondaries showing bursts from /mnt/model-cache.
deploy-bot: no recent model artifact pushes. No canary.
oncall-anna: miguel — status?
sre-miguel: rate limit applied to songbird routing rules (concurrency=2). Early signal: streaming stalls decreased in 30s. p99 dropped from 3.8s -> 2.5s in first window.
infra-ryan: lifting some cgroup throttles for pool nodes to test. Increased blkio weight for docker groups hosting model runtimes from 100 -> 500 temporarily. FYI this requires careful rollback if disk saturation increases.
ml-olivia: can we prioritize KV-cache hot objects in memory? If we bump cache size for gpt-small-q4 processes that will reduce spool-to-disk. But that might push memory pressure.
sre-miguel: we can try cached objects TTL increase for songbird only; applying patch to redis-cache policy for that tenant now.
support-lina: Customer update sent: "We detected elevated latency; we've applied temporary rate limits and are actively reducing IO contention. We expect improved streaming within minutes. We'll keep you updated." (sent to Songbird, cc: Customer Eng Jay)
customer-eng-jay: Received, Songbird acknowledges and wants ETA. They asked if we can route their traffic to a dedicated node pool for short term.
infra-ryan: We have spare capacity in dedicated-staging-gpu nodes; can migrate a small portion of Songbird traffic (~20%) as a canary. Migration script: 
```
redwoodctl route update --tenant songbird --target pool=dedicated-temp-1 --weight 20
```
I can run it if approved.
oncall-anna: Approve migration of 20% as canary. Keep rollback path ready.
infra-ryan: running migration now. Rolling 20% -> dedicated-temp-1.
ops-bot: migration event recorded. Watch for correctness and token continuity.
sre-miguel: p99 after rate-limit + blkio bump + 20% migration: 1.6s. p95 ~720ms. Stalls reduced by ~70%.
ml-olivia: good sign. Longer-term: need quota for long-context workloads or plan to invite Songbird to Dedicated tier. Opening RFC.
oncall-anna: Next steps: 1) keep migration and rate limit for 15m, monitor p95/p99 and stalls 2) if stable, gradually shift more traffic or recommend Dedicated 3) if degradations persist, cordon nodes and evict noisy containers.
infra-ryan: I'm monitoring node disk latency and blkio counters; will rollback blkio weight if host IO degrades.
sre-miguel: handoff note for next oncall: big picture — root cause likely tenant long-context causing KV cache pressure and disk IO leading to cgroup blkio throttles; mitigations applied: tenant concurrency throttle, temporary blkio weight increase, 20% shift to dedicated-temp-1, cache TTL increase. Metrics: p99 3.8s -> 1.6s.
oncall-anna: I'm going to start creating incident timeline and customer impact summary. Miguel/Ryan please add logs and exact commands to the incident doc.
sre-miguel: adding: `tc qdisc` checks, blkio counters, nvidia-smi svms, top processes, model runtime logs. Also saving `journalctl -u model-runtime` around 12:10-12:30.
infra-ryan: I'll run cordon if we see one node causing repeated bursts: `redwoodctl node cordon gpu-38` and evict containers. Not yet required.
support-lina: will keep customers updated and escalate to sales for Dedicated discussion.
oncall-anna: After 15m window, if stable, we'll start gradual rollback of blkio weight and retain routing limit until capacity plan decided. Handoff to second shift in 40m. @sre-miguel please prepare pager summary.
sre-miguel: prepping summary now, will include p95/p99 graphs, per-tenant traffic breakdown, mitigations, and next actions.
customer-eng-jay: Songbird wants a postmortem and ask whether we can avoid throttling their traffic in future; I'll coordinate capacity options.
incident-bot: INCIDENT NOTE: mitigations applied — concurrency throttle; blkio weight adjust; 20% migration to dedicated-temp-1; cache TTL bump. Continue monitoring for 30m.
oncall-anna: thanks team. I'll handoff to @sre-miguel in 40m for overnight monitoring. If any regression, repage immediately. :thumbsup:"
